facts.fact: Right ankle inversion injury playing basketball last night, landing on another player's foot.
Felt a snap, followed by rapid swelling on the outside of the ankle.
Able to walk ten to fifteen steps with a limp after the injury.
Treated with ice and elevation, and ibuprofen 400 mg this morning.
Previous left ankle sprain about two years ago; no prior injury to the right ankle.
No numbness or tingling.
Works in a warehouse.
Moderate swelling and bruising over the lateral right ankle.
Maximal tenderness over the anterior talofibular ligament.
No tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of either malleolus.
No tenderness at the base of the fifth metatarsal or the navicular.
Pulses and sensation in the foot normal.
Anterior drawer test shows mild laxity compared with the other side.
Able to bear weight for four steps in clinic.
Grade 2 lateral ankle sprain of the right ankle.
Ottawa ankle rules negative; no X-ray needed.
Elevation and ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time.
Air-stirrup brace; crutches for two or three days, weight bearing as tolerated.
Ibuprofen 400 mg every eight hours with food for up to five days.
Physiotherapy referral for balance and strengthening.
Expected three to four weeks out of basketball.
Modified duties for one week: no heavy lifting or ladders; note provided.
Return if unable to bear weight, foot becomes numb or cold, or not improving in a week.
